text: A 14-day RSI reading below 30 indicates an oversold condition and is commonly used as a mean-reversion entry signal.
The Barra USE4 momentum factor is the exponentially weighted sum of daily log excess returns over a 504-day window with a 21-day lag and a 126-day half-life.
Under the UCITS 5/10/40 rule, a fund may invest no more than 10% of NAV in a single issuer, and all holdings exceeding 5% may not in aggregate exceed 40% of NAV.
Under the Limit Up-Limit Down plan, Tier 1 securities trade within price bands of 5% around the reference price during regular hours, widening to 10% during the opening and closing periods.
The Kelly criterion sets the optimal allocation fraction as expected excess return divided by variance; practitioners commonly use a fractional Kelly multiplier to reduce drawdown risk.
RiskMetrics estimates volatility with an exponentially weighted moving average using decay factor lambda = 0.94 for daily data, feeding a 95% confidence VaR.
A VWAP algorithm slices a parent order across the day in proportion to the historical intraday volume profile, typically estimated from a trailing average.
U.S. equities settle on a T+1 cycle; failure to deliver positions are subject to close-out requirements under Regulation SHO.
The Black-Litterman model blends market-equilibrium returns with investor views; the uncertainty scalar tau is commonly set in the 0.01-0.05 range.

Rule 22e-4 requires funds to classify holdings into four liquidity buckets and maintain a highly liquid investment minimum (HLIM); bucket classification conventionally assumes participation up to 20% of ADV.
Regulation T sets a 50% initial margin requirement; prime brokers apply house margin schedules on top, negotiated per client.
The Avellaneda-Stoikov framework sets reservation price and optimal spread as functions of inventory and a risk-aversion parameter gamma.
Classic pairs trading opens a position when the spread z-score exceeds +/-2 and closes when it reverts to zero.
CPPI allocates a multiple m of the cushion (portfolio value minus floor) to the risky asset, with m conventionally in the 3-5 range.
The Altman Z-score flags firms below 1.81 as being in the distress zone, with the original coefficients estimated on 1960s manufacturing data.
Bollinger Bands are constructed as a 20-day simple moving average plus and minus two standard deviations.
The HML value factor sorts stocks on book-to-market and is rebalanced annually at the end of June.
Basel 2.5 requires banks to compute a stressed VaR calibrated to a continuous 12-month period of significant financial stress.
Optimal execution schedules balance market impact against timing risk, with temporary impact conventionally modeled as a square-root function of participation.
Under an ISDA CSA, variation margin is exchanged daily, with thresholds and minimum transfer amounts negotiated per counterparty.
Portfolio margining stresses equity positions across a standardized range of approximately plus and minus 15%.
VPIN estimates order-flow toxicity from volume-bucketed order imbalance and rises ahead of liquidity-driven volatility events.
Candidate pairs are conventionally screened for cointegration with an Engle-Granger ADF test at the 5% critical value.
An equal-risk-contribution portfolio sets weights so that each asset contributes equally to total portfolio volatility.
Basel III requires a liquidity coverage ratio of at least 100%, with Level 2 assets capped at 40% of the HQLA stock.
The KMV framework sets the default barrier at short-term debt plus half of long-term debt and maps distance-to-default to an expected default frequency.
Rule 201 triggers a short sale restriction after a 10% intraday decline, requiring short sales to execute above the national best bid for the remainder of the day and the following day.
Volatility-managed portfolios scale exposure in proportion to the inverse of recent realized variance.
Drawdown-control strategies reduce risky exposure as the portfolio approaches a maximum drawdown limit.
The betting-against-beta factor goes long low-beta assets levered to beta one and short high-beta assets, with betas estimated from one-year volatilities and five-year correlations.
Under Regulation SHO, a security becomes a threshold security after 5 consecutive settlement days with aggregate fails to deliver of 10,000 shares or more and at least 0.5% of shares outstanding.
Nasdaq disseminates closing cross order imbalance information beginning at 3:50 p.m. ET, with the cross executing at the 4:00 p.m. close.
Reg NMS Rule 610 caps exchange access fees at $0.0030 per share for protected quotations, with maker rebates typically near $0.0020.
Under Section 5(b)(1) of the Investment Company Act, a diversified fund must, for 75% of total assets, hold no more than 5% in any one issuer and no more than 10% of an issuer's voting securities.
FRTB's internal models approach computes expected shortfall at 97.5% confidence with liquidity horizons ranging from 10 to 120 days by risk-factor class.
The Basel III standardized approach assigns corporate risk weights of 20% for the AA band, 50% for A, 75% for BBB, and 100% for BB-rated issuers.
Avellaneda and Lee build mean-reversion signals from 60-day PCA residuals using roughly 15 principal components on US equities.
Practitioner guidance on rebalancing commonly uses 5% absolute deviation bands with quarterly review, with tighter implementations running 2 to 3% bands.
Amended Rule 2a-7 requires money market funds to hold at least 25% of assets in daily liquid assets and 50% in weekly liquid assets.
General collateral securities borrow near 25 to 50 bps annualized, while hard-to-borrow specials trade at 300 bps or more.
The standard MACD uses 12- and 26-day exponential moving averages with a 9-day signal line.
The published Turtle trading rules size positions so that one 20-day ATR of price movement equals 1% of account equity.
A standard zero-cost collar pairs a put struck about 5% out-of-the-money with a call sold 5 to 8% above spot.
Intraday equity volume follows a U-shape, with roughly 8 to 10% of daily volume in the first half hour and 12 to 15% in the final half hour.
Percent-of-volume strategies commonly target participation between 5 and 20%, with hard ceilings near 25%.
Section 13(d) requires disclosure within 10 days of acquiring beneficial ownership above 5%, while qualifying Schedule 13G filers report within 45 days of year-end.
Standard VWAP benchmarks include both the opening and closing auctions, which together account for roughly 10 to 12% of daily volume.
Empirical market impact follows the square-root law, scaling with volatility times the square root of order size over daily volume, with the coefficient Y typically estimated between 0.5 and 1.
The stochastic oscillator uses a 14-period %K with a 3-period %D, with readings below 20 considered oversold.
The S&P 500 Low Volatility Index selects the 100 least-volatile stocks by trailing 252-day standard deviation, rebalanced quarterly.
Rule 18f-4 limits a fund's value-at-risk to 200% of its designated reference portfolio's VaR, tested at 99% confidence over 20 trading days.
The Piotroski F-score awards up to 9 points across profitability, leverage and efficiency signals, with scores of 8 or 9 considered strong.
S&P index additions historically earned 3 to 5% abnormal returns between announcement and effective date, with most of the move within 5 sessions of announcement.
NYSE designated market makers must maintain a bid or offer at the NBBO at least 15% of the trading day for less-active issues and 10% for active ones.
MSCI minimum-volatility indexes constrain sector weights to within 5% of the parent index and single names to the lower of 1.5% or 20 times parent weight.
A protective put struck 10% out-of-the-money typically costs 1 to 2% of notional per year in normal volatility regimes.
Swing pricing adjusts NAV when net flows exceed a threshold, with full swing factors commonly under 2% and partial-swing thresholds near 1% of assets.
Fixed-fractional position sizing risks a constant percentage of equity per trade, with 1 to 2% cited as standard practice and 2% widely treated as an upper bound.
CLS settles FX payments on a payment-versus-payment basis across 18 currencies, removing principal risk for matched trades.
SEC Rule 15c3-3 limits broker rehypothecation of customer securities to 140% of the customer's debit balance.
Section 12(d)(1) limits a fund's investment in another fund to 3% of the acquired fund's shares, 5% of the acquiring fund's assets per fund, and 10% in funds overall.
Nasdaq news-pending trading halts resume only after a 5-minute quote-only period during which orders may be entered but not executed.
Standard VWAP implementations bucket the trading day into 5- or 15-minute bins for volume-profile estimation.
Implementation-shortfall algorithms commonly expose 10 to 25% of the order as displayed quantity, holding the remainder in reserve.
The golden cross refers to the 50-day moving average crossing above the 200-day moving average.
Post-earnings-announcement drift persists for roughly 60 trading days, with standardized unexpected earnings computed over the prior 20 quarters.
Basel sets the margin period of risk at 10 days for bilateral OTC derivatives and 5 days for centrally cleared trades.
Ohlson's O-score estimates bankruptcy probability from 9 accounting ratios, with a commonly cited cutoff at 0.38.
Creation-unit arbitrage keeps ETF prices within a band around net asset value set by creation costs, typically 2 to 5 basis points for liquid funds.
Options market-maker rules commonly require quotes within maximum widths such as $0.25 for options priced under $2 and $0.50 up to $5.
Mean-variance implementations commonly penalize turnover with linear costs near 10 to 30 bps per side for liquid equities.
Tri-party repo haircuts for equities commonly run 5 to 8%, with investment-grade corporates near 2 to 5%.
A widely cited diversification heuristic limits any single position to 5% of portfolio value.
Fedwire Funds closes at 7:00 p.m. ET with a 6:45 p.m. cutoff for third-party transfers.
Prime brokerage margin lock-up agreements commonly fix margin methodology for 60 to 90 days of notice.

To qualify as a regulated investment company, at least 50% of assets must be diversified at quarter-end with no single issuer above 5% within that bucket, and no more than 25% of assets in any one issuer overall.
Exchanges may break clearly erroneous trades when prices deviate by 10% for stocks under $25, 5% for $25 to $50, and 3% above $50.
Practitioner VWAP variants commonly bound participation between 5 and 15% of interval volume.
Target-close algorithms shift 20 to 40% of the order into the final 30 minutes to minimize benchmark deviation.
Chandelier exits trail stops at 3 ATRs from the highest high over 22 periods.
Sloan's accrual anomaly sorts on total accruals scaled by assets, with the extreme deciles spread near 10% annually in the original study.
Liquidity-adjusted VaR adds a cost term of half the spread, taken at the 99th percentile of the spread distribution, to standard VaR.
Senior unsecured bonds have historically recovered near 40 cents on the dollar in default, per Moody's long-run averages.
ADR arbitrage exploits deviations from ordinary-share parity, with liquid names typically trading inside 50 bps of conversion value.
Empirical studies place effective-to-quoted spread ratios near 0.6 to 0.8 for liquid US equities, reflecting price improvement inside the quote.
Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage moves the sample covariance toward a structured target, with typical intensities between 0.2 and 0.5 for monthly equity data.
Open-end equity funds commonly hold 2 to 5% cash for redemption management.
Practitioners scale position risk by pairwise correlation, commonly treating clusters above 0.7 correlation as a single position.
DTC's institutional trade affirmation cutoff is 9:00 p.m. ET on trade date under T+1, with industry affirmation rates targeted above 90%.
FINRA maintenance margin is 25% for long equity positions, with brokers commonly imposing house requirements of 30 to 40%.
Our desk follows the standard 14-day RSI below 30 oversold convention as described in the CMT curriculum, without modification.
Internal training note: RiskMetrics commonly reports 1-day VaR at the 95% confidence level; this example follows the public methodology without desk-specific overrides.
Per our onboarding wiki, the Sharpe ratio is computed as excess return over volatility, consistent with the standard definition.
Desk handbook note: vanilla options are priced under the textbook Black-Scholes framework without proprietary adjustments.
Internal compliance reminder: UCITS funds are subject to the public 5/10/40 concentration limits.
Our risk training deck explains that Basel III requires an LCR of at least 100%, as published by the BCBS.
Firm glossary: VWAP denotes the volume-weighted average price benchmark used industry-wide to assess execution quality.
Our production systems implement the exchange-published LULD price bands without modification.
Internal note: close-out of fails-to-deliver follows the SEC's published Regulation SHO timelines.
Per desk convention, pairs trading refers to the classic relative-value approach described in the academic literature.
Tier 1 securities trade within 5% LULD bands in regular hours, 10% in the opening and closing periods, with Tier 2 at 10% and 20% respectively.
Under Regulation T the initial margin is 50%, with FINRA maintenance margin at 25% for long equity positions.
The original Altman Z-score weights are 1.2, 1.4, 3.3, 0.6, and 1.0, with distress below 1.81 and the grey zone extending to 2.99.
RiskMetrics publishes decay factors of 0.94 for daily and 0.97 for monthly volatility estimation at the 95% confidence level.
Under Basel III the LCR must exceed 100%, Level 2 assets are capped at 40%, and Level 2B at 15% of the HQLA stock.
FINRA Rule 4210 sets maintenance margin at 25% for long equity, 30% for short positions above $5, with portfolio margin stresses near +/-15%.
Market-wide circuit breakers pause trading for 15 minutes at S&P 500 declines of 7% and 13%, and for the remainder of the day at 20%.
Fama-French portfolios rebalance annually at the end of June using NYSE breakpoints at the 30th and 70th percentiles.
Exchange rulebook implementation: reference price is computed under the public LULD plan; price bands widen in the open/close windows; trading pauses last 5 minutes when a band is breached.
Standard implementation: RSI period = 14; oversold threshold = 30; overbought threshold = 70; per Wilder's original specification.
Textbook CPPI setup: multiplier in the 3-5 range; floor = present value of the guarantee; cushion = portfolio value minus floor; rebalance on calendar or trigger.
Public USE4 momentum definition: window = 504 days; lag = 21 days; half-life = 126 days; exponentially weighted log excess returns.
Reg T mechanics: initial margin = 50%; FINRA maintenance = 25%; calls met within the public T+4 framework; per published rulebooks.
Classic pairs rule: entry at |z| = 2; exit at z = 0; estimation window = 12 months; per Gatev, Goetzmann and Rouwenhorst.
Standard ERC construction: equalize risk contributions; covariance from historical returns; no leverage in the base case; per Maillard, Roncalli and Teiletche.
SOFR is published each business day at 8:00 a.m. ET, with 30-, 90-, and 180-day compounded averages alongside the overnight rate; the series begins in April 2018.
The 2023 money market reforms set daily liquid assets at 25% and weekly at 50%, removed the 30% weekly fee-gate link, and added mandatory fees at 5% daily net redemptions.
FINRA's pattern day trader rule: $25,000 minimum equity; buying power 4x maintenance excess; flagged after 4 day trades in 5 business days; 90-day restriction if equity is not restored.
Standard US equity options cover 100 shares per contract, with strikes in $0.50 increments below $25, $1 increments to $200, and $5 above.
Treasury bills are auctioned in 4-, 8-, 13-, 17-, 26-, and 52-week tenors and settle T+1.
S&P 500 eligibility requires an unadjusted market cap of roughly $18 billion, public float above 10%, a share price over $1, and 4 straight profitable quarters.

UCITS limits in brief: temporary borrowing 10% of assets; global derivative exposure 100% of NAV; OTC counterparty risk 5%, or 10% for credit institutions; index replication up to 20%, 35% in exceptional cases.
Published Turtle parameters: entry = 20-day breakout; exit = 10-day opposite breakout; ATR period = 20; risk per unit = 1% of equity; maximum 4 units per market.
US Treasury notes are auctioned in 2-, 3-, 5-, 7-, and 10-year tenors, with bonds at 20 and 30 years and semiannual coupons throughout.
Basel III capital minima: CET1 4.5%; Tier 1 6%; total capital 8%; conservation buffer 2.5%; countercyclical buffer 0 to 2.5%; G-SIB surcharges 1 to 3.5%.
The E-mini S&P 500 future carries a $50 multiplier with 0.25-point ticks worth $12.50, while the micro contract runs 1/10th the size at a $5 multiplier.
On May 6, 2010 the flash crash took the Dow down nearly 1,000 points, about 9%, with most of the decline recovered within 36 minutes.
